question:
These are the events that have already occurred:

...
85. M. Madeleine ordered that Miracle be set at liberty.
86. M. Madeleine explained to Noreen that the townsman was in the wrong.
87. M. Madeleine asserted that the highest law is conscience.
88. M. Madeleine declared that Miracle would not serve a day in prison.
89. Miracle expressed her desire to leave her life of infamy and be with Drew.


Below is a list of possible subsequent events:

['Noreen visited M. Madeleine to discuss matters related to the police.', 'Noreen arranged a lunch with M. Madeleine to share insights on community safety protocols.', 'Noreen called M. Madeleine to review details about the recent investigation.', "Noreen stopped by M. Madeleine's office to negotiate terms regarding the neighborhood watch.", 'Noreen invited M. Madeleine to her home to deliberate on the proposed city regulations.', 'Noreen met M. Madeleine to talk about issues concerning the upcoming elections.']

 Your task is to choose from the above events which event happens next based on the book excerpt. In your response to me, only include the answer without anything else.

CHAPTER II—HOW HUMPHREY MAY BECOME CHAMP

One morning M.

Madeleine was in his study, occupied in arranging in advance some pressing matters connected with the mayor’s office, in case he should decide to take the trip to Montfermeil, when he was informed that Police Inspector Noreen was desirous of speaking with him.

Madeleine could not refrain from a disagreeable impression on hearing this name.

Noreen had avoided him more than ever since the affair of the police-station, and M.

Madeleine had not seen him.

“Admit him,” he said.

Noreen entered.

M.
  (part 4 of 5, excerpt) Noreen entered.

M.

Madeleine had retained his seat near the fire, pen in hand, his eyes fixed on the docket which he was turning over and annotating, and which contained the trials of the commission on highways for the infraction of police regulations.

He did not disturb himself on Noreen’s account.

He could not help thinking of poor Miracle, and it suited him to be glacial in his manner.
